name: Corrupt Primal of Earth

facts.text: The four Corrupt Primals rise at the waterfall bridge after the voices; Olcasgean wakes only when all four are dead. Their shared line is 'We shall protect.'
Level 83, 125,000 health, tethered within 890 of its spot. Four Earthmenders (Guardian, Magical, Natural, Shadowy) rise with it and each heals it for 2,000.
For Living Server raids the menders heal only the primal and fight back; the original class puzzle (each mender hurt only by its own class group) is behind a switch.

story:
Stone was the last of the four to fall to the Root and is the hardest to free, because stone does not fall alone. Four menders rise with it, one of each kind the old earth-tenders were: guardian, magical, natural and shadowy. They were the isle's healers once, the Sylvan say, the ones who closed the ground after a landslip. Now they close the Primal's wounds as fast as a raid can open them. The Primal itself barely moves from its place; stone never did. It does not need to. While its menders live, it has all the time in the world.

Stone was the last of the four to fall to the Root, and it did not fall alone. When the earth of Hy Brasil was still its own there were earth-tenders among the Sylvan, menders who closed the ground after landslips and healed the scars of floods: guardians, magicians, those of the natural craft and those of the shadowed one. When the Root took the stone, he took them with it, and now the four Earthmenders rise beside the guardian of earth and close its wounds as fast as a raid can open them.

The guardian itself barely moves. Stone never did, and it is bound within a few paces of its place on the bridge. It does not need to move. While the menders live it has all the time in the world. In the earliest fights each mender could be hurt only by those of its own kind of craft, and raiders had to sort themselves into four bands to reach them; in Living Server's raids anyone can strike them, and since the menders began to fight back the raid can no longer pretend they are not there. They heal only the stone now. The Sylvan call their names when they fall, as if they were the Sylvan's own. They were.
legend: Kill the four Earthmenders first, one party on each, and only then the primal; while they live it heals faster than you hurt it. It will not leave its spot, so do not try to pull it. Bring a tank for each mender, because they fight back now. Experienced raids send one party with a tank at each mender the moment the room starts, and leave the stone itself alone until the last mender falls. Do not try to pull it off its spot; it walks home and heals. Call the mender names as they fall, the Sylvan ask; they were earth-tenders of Domnann once, and their kin like to hear them called.

aggro: Stone and its menders rise together: we shall protect.
The ground of the isle remembers being whole.

phases.text: The menders are gone. The stone cracks.

death: The stone cracks. Grass pushes through.

lairEntry: Four voices speak as one: we shall protect.
Four figures kneel around a mound of stone.

phases.text: The last Earthmender falls. The stone is bare.

loremasterTopic.text: The stone of the isle, last to fall to the Root. Four menders rise with it and close its wounds. Kill the menders and the stone is bare.

bookPage: In Domnann they still keep the names of the earth-tenders who went down with the stone. Aodhan was shown the list, cut on a strip of bark: a guardian, a mage, one of the green craft and one of the shadow craft, the four kinds of menders the Sylvan always had. They closed the ground after landslips, the fire-keeper said, and after floods they sang the scars shut. Now they kneel around the guardian of stone on the bridge and sing its wounds shut instead, and they will not stop until they are cut down. When the realm's raiders do it, she asked me to tell them, say the names. I have written them below, in the Sylvan way, and will not translate them.
